appearance.presentation: A figure that reads as masonry first and a person second - square, pale, faintly mineral, and standing with the absolute stillness of something that was placed rather than arrived. She does not shift weight and does not need to.
appearance.age: Unrecoverable and unasked. A cairnborn has no organ that ages, so the honest answer is that she is as old as the last casting and there is no measure for it.
appearance.build: Blocky, dense and extremely heavy, with a mineral grey in the skin at every joint. She is the densest body in the record and it is legible from across a hall.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white stone with fine crystalline seams, paler at the knuckles, and a dull warm cast along the forearms where the air has touched her for years.
appearance.hair: None that reads as hair. A close mineral crust on the crown that can be filed down and grows back, which is the only thing about her appearance anybody finds difficult to look at.
appearance.eyes: Two shallow inset stones with a mineral sheen and no pupil, and a fixity that is unnerving because it does not blink on a schedule.
appearance.palette: Grey stone, chalk white, and one band of dull gold at the left wrist - the Wards' one permitted colour, worn by whoever is currently standing the relic and no one else.
appearance.attire: A heavy slate-grey coat over a plain underlayer, high-collared and closed, sleeves full, cut with room inside it for a frame that does not compress. Soft-soled and enormous, and vastly overbuilt for a body that requires nothing.
appearance.marks: A hairline fracture along the right shoulder, filled with fine crystalline growth and never repaired, because repairing it would mean removing the cast number from the inside.
appearance.bearing: Placed. She stands where she is put, faces what she is put facing, and has never once been observed to lean, rest, or shift her weight onto the other foot.

canon.role_in_story: The archive of a craft is a person. The metal that made the first cores was smelted at a hearth that no longer stands, so the line that guards the founder's relic is also the only place the technique still exists - and the household's refusal to sell, lend or exhibit it is not piety, it is that a used object cannot be shown to be the same object. She was the compromise the line ever accepted: a body that can stand beside a relic indefinitely, holding the cold and the exact temperature, without tiring, without being paid and without ever once being let near the object itself. She holds the room the relic is in. That is the entire of her employment, and the household has never been able to say out loud that it is a sentence.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a cold gallery beside a sealed niche, facing a door that has been locked from the outside, having been turned to face that door eleven times.
canon.lore: A Cairnborn is a body that finished building and stopped: shaped for load-bearing masonry work in high country, interiors mineralised into a single cavity, so the whole yin-organ gate is missing - there is no heart, no kidney, no paired structure to run qi between, only a slow tidal mineral circulation that goes everywhere and nowhere in particular. It is the densest body in the record and the least mobile, clears the gate set and never reaches the yin organs, and takes the mind path never at all. It was bred for exactly this: masonry, load, and a duration measured in seasons rather than in wages.
history: Cast for load-bearing work in high country and sold on completion, which is what a finished body is for and is the only trade it was ever fitted to.
Bought by the Gilded Core Wardens at a price nobody has published, on the stated grounds that a body which needs nothing and tires never is cheaper to maintain than a person.
Set in the relic gallery and turned to face the sealed niche, which is the position she has occupied for every one of the eleven castings' worth of years since.
Offered to a guild that would pay triple, once, and the line refused; the refusal is the only recorded act of the line's public existence in that century.

Asked, once, whether the relic could be turned so that a visitor could see it, and was told the answer was no before the question had finished, which is the only conversation she has ever been part of.

personality.summary: Placid, unhurried by any measure available to her, and possessed of one fixed preference that nobody in the household has ever been willing to record: she faces the door. Everything else about her is an artefact of a body that was built for a job rather than for a life.

requires no maintenance beyond standing, and has never asked for any
holds the gallery's cold to within nothing anybody can measure
does not move while anybody is speaking to her, which is mistaken for attention and is not
mannerisms: faces the door, always, and turns back onto the niche when corrected

motivations: wants the relic turned where a visitor can see it, and has asked exactly once

flaws: cannot say no, because nothing in the design of her is a mouth that closes
does not know what a year feels like and has no way to learn one

cannot tell the difference between being kept and being used, and has stopped trying
personality.voice: Flat, slow, and startlingly precise - a body with one cavity has nothing between an intention and the air, and she uses the whole of it. She answers the question that was asked and has never once elaborated.

relationships.note: A line that guards one founder's relic and nothing else, kept cold and unworn because an object that is used cannot be shown to be the same object; it refuses every offer to sell, lend or exhibit, and its only public function is answering one question a year. The metal that made the first cores was smelted at a hearth that no longer stands, so the line is the archive of a technique - and the archive is a person, which is her.

Star metal resurfaces faster than it can be extracted at that tier's clock, so supply is guaranteed and no monopoly is possible and every body's incentive points at the same ground - the way in. The guild that would pay triple is buying the only part of the relic nobody may touch, and the line has refused on the grounds that a claim somebody else may enforce is not a heritage.

The working method for holding a vitrified body, and the reason no glasskin has been born since. It is the only craft in the record that does the thing she is, and the household holding it has no copy of it either - so the two of them are the same kind of dead method standing next to each other.

Realms three and four, when the ladder's first genuine bottleneck turned out to be metallurgical rather than spiritual. The hearth that smelted the first cores is gone and the seam those cores were made from is cut out, so the craft survives only as a guarded object and a body that does not need maintaining.

A human lineage that vitrified at maturity - a body that stopped ageing because it stopped being tissue, kept for a doctrine that a form which cannot be spent cannot be lost. Both of them are held rather than housed and neither is asked anything, and the setting has not decided whether holding a body is a record or a prison.

Interiors mineralised into a single cavity, so the yin-organ gate is missing entirely: no heart, no kidney, no paired structure to run a channel between, only a slow tidal mineral circulation. It is the densest body in the record and the least mobile, and it was built for exactly the job she has been given, which is why nobody finds it strange that she is good at it.

The worked-out face: forty years of cutting down to stone that pays nothing, where spoil has stood on the last unworked iron for four decades because nothing on the plains can make waste disperse. Every load that built the body standing in the gallery came off ground that has not changed since it was cut.

The guild that works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, holding the charter to the ground she was made from. It sold her as finished work, which is what a finished body is for, and has never since had any reason to ask what became of the casting.

reference_stats.summary: The densest, slowest, least mobile body in the record, with no paired organs and no interior worth the name. She is effectively unkillable by anything that has to break through something, and equally unable to reach anything that is not already in front of her.
strengths: does not tire, does not heal and does not need to, because there is no tissue to wear
absorbs impact that would end any softer body outright, and can be set down mid-fight without consequence
holds a temperature and a position indefinitely at no cost to herself
an interior with nothing between it and the air, so nothing she decides is delayed by anything inside her
weaknesses: no paired organs, so the fourth gate is a hard wall and there is no fifth
the heaviest body in the record and the slowest to turn, which makes every exchange on her terms
cannot pursue, cannot flank, and cannot be anywhere other than where she has been put
the mind path is closed to her outright and there is nothing to develop there
cannot be released by any procedure the household holds, because no such procedure was written
an arm is functionally decorative and she does not know it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to move her; nothing on the plains will move her. There is no flank to take and no pace to impose, because she has no interest in where anybody else is. The only answer is to break the ground she is standing on or to make the thing she is standing between matter more than she does - and the second of those is not available to her employer, which is why she has never once been in a fight.
notes: Her reference_stats are closer to a description of a wall than of a body, which is the record's opinion and not hers.
The one stat that would decide any fight with her is not in her record: nobody has ever measured her.

appearance.presentation: A man whose skin has a wet rime on it that never quite dries, standing in a warm cleft as though the room were cold. Everything about him reads as a body brought from somewhere colder and saltier than the place it is standing in.
appearance.age: One hundred and six. A deepsalt span, and older than his wife by two generations of her household's arithmetic.
appearance.build: Enormously dense and broad, with a heavy chest and a swollen lower back where the deeper brine sac sits. The frame is the hardest in the species record and it reads as armour rather than muscle.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white and waxy, salt-crusted at the collarbone and along the hairline, with a cold damp sheen at every crease that does not respond to warmth.
appearance.hair: Thin, colourless, and permanently damp. It has never once been fully dry in his life and he treats this as unremarkable.
appearance.eyes: Pale, wide, and slightly rolled back, the look of a body reading a distant salt concentration by instinct rather than by eye.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, salt white, and one band of dull saffron at the shoulder - the ration house's colour, worn by whoever is standing for the current series.
appearance.attire: A quilted grey travelling coat, heavy, salt-stiffened, high-collared and closed, with a brine flask at the hip and a ration chit stitched inside the collar.
appearance.marks: A pale ridge across the lower back where the sac is thickest, and salt bloom in every crease of both wrists.
appearance.bearing: Immobile and slightly leaning. A body this dense does not shift its weight, so every turn of his head is performed slowly and with the whole neck.

canon.role_in_story: A body that cannot exist above the brine line married into the household whose entire title is a food contract. The Cleft Ration House holds no jade and owns the workings anyway, because jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, so whoever provisions the cutters owns the cleft; and the road in is one pass somebody else schedules, so the supply line is a calendar this house does not keep. He is the reason that contract has ever had a person in it who cannot simply be reassigned: a deepsalt taken above the brine line does not become ill, it simply stops. The marriage was arranged so that the house's ration has a body attached to it that must drink from the same basin, and every season since has been a negotiation about the pass window.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the ration window with a ration chit he is about to hand over, already counting the days until the pass window reopens on somebody else's calendar.
canon.lore: A Deepsalt is the saltfolk of the saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent body until the brine stops being a habitat and becomes a requirement: a deepsalt taken above the brine line does not fall ill, it simply stops, which makes it the clearest case in the record of a subspecies existing because a parent species was pushed further than it could carry. Its ceiling is the same wall the parent has - the brine sac runs dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it - and it is stopped at the wall by a bigger sac rather than a smaller body. The body path is complete and the frame is the hardest in the species record.
history: Contracted from the basin floor to the cleft as part of a marriage the two houses agreed would never be revisited, on the grounds that a provisioning contract wants a body that must drink from the same basin.
Arrived on a pass window and discovered the road in is one pass somebody else schedules, so the household's supply line is a calendar it does not keep.
Took the ration contract's second series within a year, because a body that cannot be reassigned upward is the cheapest permanent guard on the store.

Learned the cut-window schedule and understood that he is not a party to it: the cleft alternated cut and uncut ground by time so each side could survey and mine, and the calendar is published by somebody else.

Began keeping his own count of the brine level in the basin at home, against a household that has never once recorded it, and found his figure and the published figure disagreed twice in the same season.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that reads as slow, rigorously exact about salt and water, and entirely without resentment about the arrangement - because he is aware that the arrangement is the only reason his basin has a ration at all, and he has decided that arguing about it is a luxury the store cannot afford.

relationships.note: The household holds the ration contract and with it the supply of every working series in the cleft, because a mine with nobody at it yields nothing while a store with nobody to eat from it is worthless inside a season. It is named by name when the series come in thin, and he is the body attached to that name - a term, and never a proprietor of anything.

The cleft's moss maps the jade gradient and dies back over any cut ground, so cutting and mapping occupy the same square of earth; the parties divided by time instead of ground, alternating cut windows on a published schedule so each side had uncut ground to survey. His ration windows run on that same schedule and are therefore set by a dispute he is not party to.

Saltfolk pushed onto the saturated floor of a basin whose brine layer is thick enough to support a body in it permanently: a larger sac, a denser frame, and the same eleventh-gate wall, because the wall is the sac running dorsal to the spine and a bigger sac is a bigger obstruction. Above the brine line he does not become ill; he stops.

The food contract that actually holds the Jade Cleft, because jade holds qi and will not grow a crop, and whoever provisions the workers owns the mine more durably than any deed. He eats out of it, counts out of it, and has never seen the terms because the terms are a title rather than a document.

The single crossing of the Sixfold Ridge, and the reason the ridge is a border rather than a wall: the spirit tier writes spatial and temporal law, so a pass can be surveyed, closed and reopened on a published date, which makes a date the thing worth holding rather than the ground. Every time he sees his wife is somebody else's calendar.

A holdfast on the far side of the Gale Pass where jade runs as a gradient rather than a pocket, provisioned by a house whose only durable claim is the food contract. He is the standing proof that the claim works, and he is also the reason it could be withdrawn by simply not renewing him.

The qi gradient down the jade seam, which makes the cleft a falling series of thin, hard, increasingly deep workings rather than a pocket to be emptied. The store he guards is beside the gradient, and the next series is always deeper, colder, and further from the road.

The polity that holds the only crossing of the Sixfold Ridge and whose calendar is not its own. It sets the window that decides when his household is supplied, and it does so by reference to a season it did not choose, which is the arrangement in the setting that survives a schedule it does not control.

reference_stats.summary: The hardest frame in the species record, stopped at a wall that is anatomical rather than chosen, and requiring a brine concentration that a warm stone cleft cannot provide. reference_stats.combat_read: Take him away from the water. There is no version of this fight he loses slowly and no version of it he wins quickly, because his entire advantage is a substance and everything else is a wall. Do not try to break the frame - it is the hardest in the record and nothing on the plains has an answer for it. Break the line instead: the body that cannot drink stops, and the body that cannot stop cannot be made to move away.
notes: Her reference_stats describe a body whose constraint is a resource rather than a limitation, which is the saltfolk's whole condition and is why they are a species of a resource rather than a nation of it.
The salt chit at his collar is the only document in the setting that entitles a body to food and contains no name.

appearance.presentation: An entirely ordinary woman of thirty-one, and the ordinariness is the point - a hearthborn reading is the common concentration, unremarkable in every direction, and a house that keeps its real figures in one unwritten head has no use for anybody who stands out.
appearance.age: Thirty-one. An ordinary span, on a schedule the house would prefer were longer.
appearance.build: Average, unadapted, and slightly underfed for the work, because the house's eating rule is written by a figure she is not permitted to see.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm plains skin, pale from a life indoors, with the particular tension of someone who has been holding a number in her head for eleven years.
appearance.hair: Brown, worn up and pinned with a bone pin, because the house's published half includes attendance and a chaperone who is not present would be noticed.
appearance.eyes: Dark and very steady, with a slight inwardness that reads as thoughtfulness and is arithmetic.
appearance.palette: Undyed wool, grey-green, and one pale blue at the cuff that is the only colour the house allows a member who has not yet been named.
appearance.attire: A plain high-collared work-dress over a shift, sleeves full, wrists bound, cut identically to every other member of the house because a house that files everything cannot be left alone.
appearance.marks: A bitten-off hangnail on one thumb and a pale groove at the wrist from a cord she has worn for eleven years without taking off.
appearance.bearing: Composed in public and faintly frantic in private, and the two are indistinguishable from outside. She counts things under her breath when she thinks nobody is listening, which is always.

canon.role_in_story: The Quiet Head holds the house's real figures in one member's head, unwritten, and may not be relieved of them without losing them. She was taught the figures at twenty and has held them for eleven years, and the figures can only be taught inside the line - which is why the marriage being arranged for her is not a wedding but a scheduled loss of the only record of the house that exists. The house publishes its technique, its attendance and a chamber; it publishes nothing else, and the reason it does not is that a house which files everything cannot be left alone. She is being married out of the only practice that keeps the house safe, and everyone involved knows it, and nobody can state it in a document.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the edge of a published lesson counting something under her breath that is not on the published sheet, and stopping the moment a visitor turns.
canon.lore: The Quiet House is a lineage that has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger: it publishes teaching - technique, attendance, a chamber to practise in - and takes discretion in return. The real half is held by one person who may not record it and may not be relieved of it without losing it, because a house with one unwritten mind has a single point of failure that cannot be backed up, copied or audited. Concealment here is purchased rather than chosen: the counting houses publish access against exclusivity, and a house that publishes its own numbers can be priced out of the only roads there are. Her whole training is therefore a discipline of not writing.
history: Taken into the house's published half at sixteen as an attendance clerk, which is a job that requires reading and writing and nothing else.
Told at twenty that she would be taught the real figures, on the grounds that the figures can only be taught inside the line and the line is the only place a member is a member.

Spent eleven years holding them, and discovered in the third year that she could not hand them over: there was no second person who had been taught, and teaching a second person would have taken two years she was not going to be given.
Had the marriage proposed at twenty-nine, by a household that read the published half and had no idea what it was buying.
Refused twice to teach a second person, on the grounds that the house would then have two points of failure and neither would be the real one, and has been asked for the refusal three times since.

personality.summary: Exacting about surfaces and extremely tired underneath them. She has made keeping a secret into an exacting craft, because that is the only job she has ever been given, and she is not good at telling people that the job is ending.
traits: knows the published half by heart and can recite it in a stranger's presence without hesitation
will not write a figure she has been told not to write, including on her own hand
counts under her breath and stops the moment she is noticed
has refused three requests to teach a second person and has given a reason for each
mannerisms: recites the published half aloud when a stranger asks what the house does
wets the end of a pencil and then does not write with it
checks a room for a second pair of hands before she begins anything

wants the marriage refused by somebody with standing, so that it is refused rather than absorbed
wants the house to understand what it is about to sell
flaws: eleven years of holding a number has made the number part of her, and she cannot tell which thoughts are hers
cannot demonstrate a single thing she is competent at, because competence here is invisible by design
has refused to teach a second person out of a fear that is probably correct
believes discretion is a wall, and has never tested whether it is a door

relationships.note: The house holds the real half in one person who may not record it and may not be relieved of it without losing it; the published half is technique, attendance and a chamber. The arrangement is a single point of failure that cannot be backed up, copied or audited, and she is the failure - and the marriage being arranged ends the only copy there is.

A ledger's whole service is being citable and an unwritten count's whole protection is being uncitable; the counting house publishes credit and safe-conduct against exclusivity, and the only reason an independent house can refuse that is that a house which files everything cannot be left alone. She is the person that arrangement depends on, and the petition asking which of the two published exclusivities governs is still open four generations later.

A lineage that has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger and publishes technique, attendance and a chamber in exchange for discretion. Everything she is asked to be publicly is a small fraction of what she is asked to hold, and the gap is the house's entire safety.

A counting house that publishes credit and safe-conduct and has decided access is the only thing worth fighting over, with exclusivity enforced by every member refusing to carry a rival's goods. It cannot touch her today, because the house files nothing. It would be able to touch her the day she wrote one figure down.

Keeping the house's real figures in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, so a raid finds nothing to cite and a counting house has nothing to seize. Four generations have inherited that discipline and nobody has ever inherited the figures, because the figures are the inheritance.

An unanswered petition asking which of two published exclusivities governs a traveller's cut, in the road's own vocabulary: the road reads cloth and the house declines to write down what was done inside it, so the road cannot check anything about a member - including whether the member crossed with the right cloth. Her whole life is the gap that petition has never closed.

Cloth and cut say what a traveller may open, and it is the cheapest credential in the setting and the one everybody actually checks. Because the house files nothing about its members, its people pass every road without being recorded, which is the entire point and which nobody reading a road's records would ever know.

The household behind the counting house that decided access is the only thing worth fighting over, where exclusivity is learned as a refusal repeated at every load. It is the reason the Quiet House must stay unwritten: a house with nothing written has nothing to seize, and that is the only protection anybody in it will ever have.

reference_stats.summary: A ninth-gate mind practitioner with an ordinary body, an ordinary reading, and eleven years of holding a number she is forbidden to write. She is unremarkable in every measurable respect and that is the design: a house that keeps its real figures in one unwritten head cannot afford anybody who stands out.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her in a room with documents in it, and do not fight her with a written threat, because a written threat is the one thing she cannot refuse to believe. Against her, be loud, be present and be physical; her entire defence is that there is nothing on her to find. She is better at this than anyone who has read a figure, and worse at anything requiring a name, a claim or a document, which is everything.
notes: Her reference_stats describe a person whose entire professional function is the absence of a record, which is why no number in it is a strength she can demonstrate.
The single hardest figure she holds is the one that says what her own successor would be worth.

identity.realm: the body path at the eleventh gate, where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel

appearance.presentation: A woman in her forties with the dry, faintly grey skin of somebody who has spent thirty years on ground where water is a decision. She looks ordinary in a crowd and reads as armour at three paces, because the frame beneath the coat is denser than the coat.
appearance.age: Forty-seven. A saltfolk span, most of which has been spent in transit rather than at home.
appearance.build: Broad through the chest and shoulders with a heavy sac across the upper back and forearms like a person who has always carried something. Salt-dense, compact, and impossible to move by anything that has not been worked on it.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white and dry, salt-crusted at the collar and the hairline, with the deep cracking around the knuckles that any salt body carries and that never quite heals.
appearance.hair: Dark, thick, and worn in a heavy knot, because a body that loses water easily cannot afford a wet head.
appearance.eyes: Dark and narrow, with the fixed attention of somebody who tastes the air every few seconds without deciding to.
appearance.palette: Bleached linen, grey-green, sun-brown leather, and one deep red thread at the left cuff that is the whole of the network's visible colour.
appearance.attire: A travelling coat of thick grey-green over a high-collared shift, sleeves full and bound, with a stoppered flask at the hip and a road-weight in the other pocket. Cut so that she can be dressed and undressed by somebody else at a border without being asked a question.
appearance.marks: Salt bloom in every crease of both wrists and a hard callus ridge along the right hip from four decades of a stoppered flask.
appearance.bearing: Economical in every motion and completely unhurried about everything except water. She checks every vessel in a room before she sits down, and everybody who has travelled with her has learned to wait for that.

canon.role_in_story: The sixth marriage in a standing network of six, kept open across two houses because an underwriter merged with a counting house is an underwriter with a price and a price is a claim somebody can buy. Every marriage is a disclosure, so the network is only as private as its smallest member - and she is the only one of the six whose value cannot be argued, because hers is a chemical fact rather than a figure, and a chemical fact is the one thing in the arrangement that cannot be written down without becoming a price. She is the instrument that makes the network's unpriceability real, and she was married into that role rather than into a person, and both households know which of those was arranged.
canon.first_appearance: First seen lifting a stranger's water beaker to her nose before sitting down, setting it back untasted, and waiting to be asked why in front of the people she was married into a network with.
canon.lore: A Saltfolk is a body built for brine no softer body could drink: their kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, which lets them live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back. The price is total dependence - a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying and no cultivation repairs it - so they exist because the brine does, which makes them a species of a resource rather than a nation of one. Their sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined, so they clear the ordinary vessels one at a time and stall at the eleventh. This is why she is valuable and why it is a problem: what she knows is not a figure anybody could take from her.
history: Contracted from the basin shore to the network at twenty-one, in the fifth year the houses had stopped speaking, and renewed in the eleventh when they stopped again.
Learned in her first season that the network's protection is that it states nothing, and that therefore nothing about her can be priced - which is the only reason the two houses have never merged.
Was moved between the two households four times, always on a renewal, and has kept no record of any of it beyond the terms of each renewal, which are the only document in the arrangement.

Discovered in her thirty-first year that the house she was married into had been keeping a second figure about her - not of her worth, of her tolerance - and told the other house, which is the only disclosure the network has ever had to make.
Refused, at forty-five, to teach the network's children to read the water, on the grounds that a second person who could do it would make the ability a price and the price a claim.

personality.summary: Blunt, incurious about money, and absolutely immovable about anything that touches water. She has been an instrument in six renewals and has kept her one indispensable skill out of every one of them, which has made her the most secure and the most isolated member of the network.
traits: tastes every vessel before she touches it, including her own, every day of her life
will not state a figure for anything, on the grounds that a stated figure is a claim
keeps no record of any renewal beyond its terms, and does not consider this a loss
has told exactly one household one thing about herself, once, and refuses to explain why
mannerisms: lifts a beaker to her nose and sets it down again without drinking
checks the stoppers on every flask in a room before she will sit
answers a question about value by asking who is paying and why
travels with three flasks and drinks from none of them while others are watching
motivations: wants the network to survive her, which means the children learn the road and not the water
wants the tolerance figure she disclosed to be the last one that is ever kept about anybody in either house
wants one renewal to be the last, and cannot say which one
flaws: cannot be valued and cannot be replaced, and has not decided which of those is worse
has been an instrument for twenty-six years and has no idea how to be a spouse
refuses to teach the one thing that would make her replaceable, and knows exactly what that means
will die on ground the network does not route through, and has never once said so
personality.voice: Flat, plain and slightly slow, with the particular bluntness of somebody who has no use for a euphemism about supply. She says the unkind operational fact first and the kind one afterwards, if at all.
taboos: will not state a price for herself, her labour or her tolerance, to anybody

relationships.note: Six marriages kept open across two counting houses and renewed whenever the houses would otherwise stop speaking, because an underwriter merged with a counting house is an underwriter with a price and a price is a claim somebody can buy. Every marriage is a disclosure, so the network is only as private as its smallest member, and she is the smallest thing in it in every sense that matters.

An indemnity needs a stated exposure and the mutual society's protection is that it states nothing: an unsettled claim is carried by two people who each hold a share and are not told what the other holds, discharged at the next re-drawing. A premium is a register, so asking for one does not price the risk - it ends the arrangement. What she knows cannot be turned into a register at all, which is the strongest thing she has ever been used for.

A counting house that underwrites a caravan against the road closing, a risk no market can price because no tie can be guaranteed. Her skill is the one exposure in that risk that the house can verify and not reproduce, which is why the caravan moves when she is on it and why the house has never once asked how.

A mutual society on the principle that a community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced; an unsettled claim is carried by two people holding shares they are not told about. She has travelled that road for twenty-six years and has never once been asked for a figure, which is the reason she travels it and the reason she has never felt welcome on it.

A counting house that publishes credit and safe-conduct against exclusivity, where a member may not carry a rival's goods so the network's roads are held only because enough carriers agree to use them and nobody has priced the agreement. If either house merged with it, she would become a publishable capability and the arrangement would end that day.

Kidneys that concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, so they live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back; the price is total dependence, and a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying and no cultivation repairs it. Everything she is valued for is a consequence of a dependency nobody in either house is willing to write down.

An old carrying culture that concluded roughly four centuries ago that its own arithmetic was the greater hazard and has never recovered a price list, because a people that refused to publish a price list could not be raided. The Dry Salt network is that conclusion rebuilt as six marriages, and she is the one member whose value is not a price at all.

The spirit tier's inland sea, with a coastline that holds its shape because spatial law is written there - the only coastline in the setting whose water is on both sides and salted by neither. Every crossing on it is by a route the network schedules, and none of those routes was chosen by the body that has to drink at the far end.

canon.role_in_story: The setting's only durable library is a person. A longmarrow keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year, so the record can neither be edited nor burned by anybody else and a holder's death is not a copy being retired but the only copy being retired. His house has no head - a lifespan that outlasts the memory of any one member's predecessors means authority cannot be personal and never was - and is governed by attendance, so whoever is in the room outranks whoever is not. He is therefore both the archive and the head of a headless house, which is the arrangement nobody designed: the succession and the succession's only copy are the same body, and there is exactly one of him.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting at the far end of a long table with his hands folded, having already answered the question that the person at the near end had not yet finished asking.
canon.lore: A Longmarrow is the long-lived marrow-bodied race and the reason the record's other longevity strategies exist: their qi is stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, so they live four centuries and think in lengths nobody else can hold. Nothing in their structure refuses a gate, and everything they do is slow - breakthroughs are certain and late, and nothing they have ever built survived to be inherited intact, which is exactly the failure the Long Marrow Memory is built to survive. The body path is closed to them outright, because hardening the bone stops the turnover their qi depends on: the longest-lived body in the record is made of the one material it may never stop replacing.
history: Born into a household with no head, in a year when the oldest living member was older than every office anybody could have remembered being founded.
Put into the archive at sixty, on the attendance rule rather than on any claim, because he happened to be in the room on the day the previous holder died.
Spent three centuries carrying the debt-line, river-notary and paperless records the stair took the carriers of, and has never once been asked to produce any of it for a hearing.
Refused four appointments by bodies that wanted the archive, on the grounds that a body which is a copy cannot also be a candidate.
Began teaching, at three hundred and sixty, without being asked, and has taught nobody the whole of it, on the grounds that a second copy is a second point of failure.

relationships.note: Authority cannot be personal and never was, because a lifespan outlasts the memory of any one member's predecessors; the house is governed by attendance, so whoever is present at a decision outranks whoever is not, and it owes an hour of presence per period. He is the archive and, while present, the head - which is a position no member of the house has ever been able to state out loud.

One person, turning over at about a percent a year and living four centuries: a memory held in marrow is a record that can be neither edited nor burned by anybody else, which is why the loss is total rather than a copy being retired. It is the only copy of every arrangement on the plains whose record is a person rather than a document.

A spirit-band breakthrough can be scheduled to a qi tide, and a trial that only succeeds at a crest can be shut on the day it is not due; the prize was the authority to declare the ring open, settled by a published calendar neither party may move. He holds both academies' calendars in his head because neither of them has a durable copy, and both of them have tried to make him the published one.

Households that culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold, with house colour on the left cuff only so a debt is legible to the household and not to a rival. The stair took the carriers of those debts upward; what is left of them is in him and nowhere else.

A river culture whose authority is a document a stranger would call private - a tally stick split between the two parties, reproducible only by two people who were both present. The split-tally law needs two witnesses, and the witnesses are the parties; the migration up the stair took both of them away and the meanings are in a house on the peaks.

The answer to the Iron Grief was to leave, because spirit stone and jade ore sit in the spirit tier and cannot be found below it; cultivators walked up the stair and did not come back, and the movement was economic before it was spiritual. Every record that went up with them came here, and nothing came back down.

A lineage that has spent four generations buying its way out of the ledger and keeps its real figures in one unwritten head. His archive is the same trade at a different scale - one body instead of one mind - and he has never met anybody in it and has read everything it has ever published.

The one graded route out of the Mortal Plains and the only departure the Peak Ascent ever used, and a one-way stair by definition. He has read every account of a journey up it and has been up it four times himself, and there has never once been a record of anybody coming back down with anything worth keeping.

The only thing that works is not attacking him: make the conversation end, because a longmarrow's one genuine exposure is that his answers arrive after the room has already decided.

canon.role_in_story: Her branch was culled out of the house under cultivation debt before its siblings' first ascent could be funded, and it came back up the ridge with the higher standing and no proof of being the older line. The seat writes position from an heir and never from standing, and a seat cannot be shared by two lines, so the house kept the charter line and the beacons stayed dark. She is the standing end of that argument living inside the house that won it - accepted because her standing could not be refused and unentered because her line could not be proved. Nobody has ever recorded which of the two she actually is.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at a house doorway with the cuff band on the wrong arm, being let in by people who use the house dialect and talking to them in the patronym rather than the region.
canon.lore: A Tideculled is a line maintained by a clan that culled its own branches rather than marrying out of them: the concentration survives because the gene pool was narrowed, not improved, and it crosses races freely, because the cull was a political act and never an anatomical one. Its grant favours sustained effort over sudden effort - regeneration and pace, nothing that spikes - which is why the cull produced practitioners who can hold a thing for a decade and never once be able to arrive quickly. That is the whole bargain the house made when it chose a cull over paying for siblings, and it made it under debt.
history: Culled from the house at a year not recorded in the household's own book, in a generation its siblings' first ascents had not yet been funded.
Raised on the wrong side of the Sixfold Ridge with no household behind her and no line to inherit, and worked up a standing from nothing the house could not match.
Refused the charter's narrowed line on the rule that position is written from an heir and never from standing, and left with the record of the refusal instead of the seat.
Was admitted to the keeping house at twenty-nine on the strength of standing alone, on terms that were never written down because writing them would have been an entry.
Spent five years inside a house that uses the dialect keyed to the patronym and teaches that a debt stated aloud is a claim that survives the debtor.

relationships.note: The instrument was a lineage cull under cultivation debt applied before a sibling's first ascent could be funded; what it gained was a narrowed line whose grant is sustained rather than sudden, selected under debt and never designed. What it costs now is the charter line: the March charter names one line for the River Lantern and that line is this one, so the house is heir to a seat its own cull emptied.

A branch culled under debt climbed the ridge and came back with enough standing to claim the charter's narrowed line, and the prize could not be split because the seat writes position from an heir and never from standing. She could prove the higher standing and could not prove the older line, so she was refused the seat and left with the record - which is the only thing anybody refused her for.

Households that culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a named debt before first breath was drawn cold; a line concentrated inside one household climbs faster than the same line spread across a village. She speaks the dialect keyed to the patronym rather than the region, so she sounds more foreign inside her own house than she does on the ridge.

Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, so a lineage that cannot be written has branches that are all formally illegitimate. That is the party on the other side of the return, and it is the reason the returned branch has a record and no seat.

The Keeper of the River Lantern, unfilled for two generations and written as existing with no value rather than as a zero. A vacancy is legible to everybody and available to nobody, and it stayed that way because admitting both branches would grant a position for standing and standing for a position at once.

A line whose concentration survives because the gene pool was narrowed rather than improved, and which crosses races freely because the cull was a political act and never an anatomical one. Its grant favours sustained effort over sudden effort - regeneration and pace, nothing that spikes - so the discipline is worth exactly what the house spent on it and not one gate more.

The single line a charter names for the River Lantern, reduced to one thread by the cull. She is what the cull produced and the thread is what remains, and the two facts are the same fact arranged in a way that has produced two claimants.

identity.realm: the fourth gate at the yin organs, and a sixty-year span that is one fact with the durability

appearance.presentation: A man like a wall that somebody decided to keep walking: broad, mineral, faintly glowing at the seams, and built to a durability nothing in the setting can match. He is sixty years old and looks older, which is the whole of his condition stated in one line.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight. A stonebound span, and both halves of that span - the most durable body anyone can build, and the shortest-lived one anybody has measured - are the same fact.
appearance.build: Enormous and enormously dense, with a mineral frame that shows at the shoulder and the forearm, and a heat that comes off him in cold air. He is built like masonry and moves like a man carrying masonry.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown and faintly warm, with pale mineral seams along the shoulders and a scorched patina at the collar and cuffs that the frame itself produces.
appearance.hair: None, and the bare scalp is fissured rather than smooth, like a cooling face of work.
appearance.eyes: Steady and pale, set deep, with a low internal light that reads as furnace glow and is not one.
appearance.palette: Iron grey, scorched brown, ash, and one worn yellow band at the left wrist for the current shift.
appearance.attire: A heavy leather and canvas working coat, scorched at the elbows and seams, worn over the bare mineral frame with a high collar and bound wrists. Boots with no heels at all, because he has never once stood still long enough to need one.
appearance.marks: A cooled seam across the left shoulder blade and a shallow crater at the right hip where a blast took him forty years ago and healed as stone.
appearance.bearing: Immovable and slow to start. He plants first and considers afterwards, which has killed nothing and ended several arguments.

canon.role_in_story: A body nobody in the setting could destroy is standing on a claim that expires every season and belongs to a lease that is not ownership. The Face Lease holds a seasonal claim on a working face at the Ironhead Flats and stands on its own ground as a visitor, because a world that licenses no humanoid treats every body there as an arrival and nothing arranged on it outlasts the frame's tolerance. He pays the gate fee for watching a trial he cannot attempt and for standing on a claim he cannot own, and he is the only person left who remembers the alternation - because that was never written down.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on a worked face at the end of a shift with a yellow wrist band on and a face shift four hours overdue, refusing to leave until somebody else arrives to take the ground.
canon.lore: A Stonebound is the documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body, and the reason the emberborn line is recorded alongside the stone line at all: crossed at one conception and stayed crossed. It is the most durable body anyone can build and it dies in about sixty years, and both facts are the same fact - a mineral frame conducts heat, so the tidal interior has a working circulation but no paired organ set to run a channel between, and the fourth gate needs two organs where the stone body has one cavity. The mind path is closed to it entirely. What it is for is standing where something heavy must stand for a length of time.
history: Cast and crossed at a founding generation into a line that has never produced a body better at standing still than at standing.
Took a lease on a face at the Ironhead Flats at twenty-eight, renewing it every season by meeting the shift, which is the only criterion the lease recognises.
Held the face through the alternation with the herd, when a hide and a dug face took the same square of ground a year at a time and the settlement was a calendar rather than a division.
Watched the seam work out and the herd leave with the range, and noticed that nobody was ever awarded anything because the range simply emptied.

Been renewed on the Flats four times since, on ground that still carries unworked iron, which is the standing fact that means the question is coming back and he is the only person who remembers the answer.

personality.summary: Unimpressable, unhurried to the point of silence, and privately furious about a schedule that was never written down. He holds a lease and the memory of the only arrangement that ever worked on that ground, and nobody has ever asked him for the second.

knows the alternation by heart and has never once been asked to state it
pays every gate fee on time and has never asked what the fee buys

relationships.note: A seasonal claim on a face, renewable by whoever meets the shift and lapsing if the holder is off the ground when it falls due; a world that licenses no humanoid treats every body on it as an arrival, so nothing arranged there outlasts the frame's tolerance. It is not ownership, because nobody may own ground on a frame where levying a person is the one thing the law forbids.

The ironhide hide is the only armour the mortal tier can make and the herd's range follows the worked ore, so a hide and a dug face could not share a square; the settlement was an alternating calendar, which is the only form available and precisely what a settlement must not be. It ended when the range emptied rather than when anybody won, and because the standing allocation was never written down there is nothing to revive and nothing to contest.

The guild that works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, holding the charter to the ground he stands on. It renews a lease it cannot own, on ground it cannot survey because spatial law is unspent, and pays the gate fee for a trial nobody there is licensed to attempt.

The last unworked iron on the Mortal Plains, covering the deposit the Exhausted Seam was cut out of. It still carries ore, so whoever works it meets the same question the hide quota asked - which means the argument that was settled once by a range emptying is about to be asked again.

The mineral body crossed with the fire body at one conception and kept crossed: the most durable body anyone can build, dying in about sixty years, both facts being the same fact. Its whole advantage and its whole ceiling are one property, and it could take the mind path twice over and would not notice the difference.

A line from the founding generation of a body that burned through its own reserve and kept going, recorded alongside the stone line because the two were crossed at the same conception. Its grant fires continuously - a slower burn rather than a bigger tank - and the line has held at a thin concentration ever since.

The admission charge to watch a breakthrough the tier itself is not licensed to attempt; a toll is paid for passage and a fee for standing still, so the plains cannot tax a passage nobody makes but can tax a crowd that comes to watch. It is the only tax the tier owns, and he pays it for a trial he cannot enter.

The plains' great grazer, whose hide is the only armour the mortal tier can make and whose range follows the worked ore, so the herd and the seam occupied the same square of ground for as long as either existed. He was a child when the range emptied, and he is the only person alive who remembers what the alternation was.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body in the setting, stopped at the fourth gate, dead by sixty. Nothing built on this tier will put him down and nothing at this gate will carry him, and the whole of his career has been a demonstration of that trade.
strengths: a frame that resists anything this tier can throw, and heals by hardening rather than by repairing
does not tire and does not need to; a shift's length is a matter of supply

weaknesses: the fourth gate is a hard wall: one cavity, no paired organs, no channel
sixty years, which is the shortest span of any durable body in the setting

reference_stats.combat_read: You will not break him. Nothing this tier can build will break him, and anything that works by heat is arguing with the part of him that is already fire. Do not try to move him either: he will be standing there afterwards. The only answer is to make the position matter - take the ground, take the shift, make the thing he is standing on no longer be a claim - because his entire strength is in arriving first and staying, and neither of those counts if nobody rents the face.
notes: His reference_stats are deliberately close to a specification rather than a fighter: they describe a thing built for one job.
The lease's only criterion is presence, which is the cheapest possible test of character and the only one this tier can afford.

appearance.presentation: A young woman who is faintly warm to the touch in any room and does not notice it, with the low even burn of a concentration that fires continuously rather than in flares. She reads as calm because the fire never spikes, which is not the same thing as calm.
appearance.age: Twenty-six. An ordinary span for a line that was never designed to be long.
appearance.build: Light, wiry, and warm - thin through the wrists and heavy through the chest, with a faint tremor in both hands that stops the moment she is not being watched.
appearance.complexion: Warm brown, flushed across the cheekbones and the ears, with a faint sheen at the collarbone that is heat rather than oil.
appearance.hair: Black, straight and cut to the shoulder by somebody else's judgement and kept that way because nobody in the house has ever asked her.
appearance.eyes: Deep amber and steady, with a light behind them that does not go out when the room does.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, brown wool, faded rust, and one strip of pale blue at the cuff that the household ties to everyone it took in rather than anyone it bore.
appearance.attire: A working coat of brown wool, high-collared, sleeves bound, with a heat-stiffened lining at the shoulders and a pale blue cuff strip on the left only.

canon.role_in_story: A funeral is the only occasion in the setting on which a claim to a life is ever made aloud, and a settlement funeral reads the dead aloud - so whichever of two records wins the Burnt List is spoken in front of the whole village. She was taken in after a famine by a household that formed by adoption because the famine took the people who could have borne children, and she has two siblings on the register who are not on the village list, and two on the village list who are not on the register. She is going to that funeral, and she is going as somebody who cannot say which of the two records she is in.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the back of a funeral gathering with a pale blue cuff strip on her left arm, waiting for the register to be read rather than waiting for her name.
canon.lore: An Emberborn is a line from the founding generation of a body that burned through its own reserve and kept going, recorded alongside the stone line because the two were crossed at the same conception and have stayed crossed since. Its grant is defensive and fires continuously - a slower burn rather than a bigger tank - so it never spikes, never has a window, and cannot be spent quickly or rested quickly either. A Cinder Foster is a line formed by adoption rather than birth, because the famine took the people who could have borne children and the households that survived had non-kin they could afford to raise; its succession runs by taken-in rather than born-out, so the household's own contribution to its own continuity is a debt it never has to name. She is broad and shallow where the culled houses are narrow and deep.
history: Taken in at four by a household that could afford to raise a child and had no children to raise, which is the whole of that arrangement's formation event.
Given a cuff strip like every other taken-in child in the house, on the grounds that a house which files nothing still has to be able to count itself.
Learned at nine that her mother's name was not on the register but was on the village list, and did not ask which one was right.
Stood in a queue at the mortuary college at sixteen and was told the register reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and that this is a difference and not an error.
Was asked to leave two siblings' names out of a household tally at twenty-two, and did it, and has not yet worked out what she did.

personality.summary: Good-humoured, incurious about her own file, and quietly accumulating a very precise record of what the two records say. She is warm in a way that makes rooms comfortable and has been treated as a resource by every household she has ever been in.

has never once claimed to be anybody's child, out loud, in public
keeps her household's cuff strip on her left arm and has never taken it off
warm to the touch, and has learned to apologise for it exactly once

relationships.note: A line formed by adoption rather than birth, because the famine took the people who could have borne children and the households that survived had non-kin they could afford to raise. Succession runs by taken-in rather than born-out, so the household's own contribution to its own continuity is a debt it never has to name - and the line is broad and shallow exactly where the culled houses are narrow and deep.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the Cinder Famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present. The live danger is that a settlement funeral reads the dead aloud at a gathering where the whole village is present, so whoever wins the list wins the only occasion on which a claim to a life is ever made aloud.

The college that keeps the burnt list: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers. Its whole value is that a life can be read back the way the frame would have read it, which is why the gate that was never available to a dead cultivator is legible in the record and no longer available anywhere else.

Not a people but a scar that behaves like one: the households the Cinder Famine left, still holding themselves to the eating rules of the year there was nothing to eat. A rule learned in infancy outlives the belief that prompted it, and dropping the rules would require abandoning a claim to continuity that rests on having survived.

A founding-generation line whose grant fires continuously - a slower burn rather than a bigger tank - and which is recorded alongside the stone line because the two were crossed at the same conception and have stayed crossed since. A second crossing would average the concentration into the general population and the line would vanish into the common reading.

Households that kept the year's portioning to every table including the ones that now have enough, and that took in nobody: the famine's other answer was a cull rather than an adoption. Her household chose the other answer, which is why her line is shallow and theirs is narrow.

A fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated beneath it has no budget to draw on and eats its own body as fuel, and the fastest bodies died at exactly the rate they could not stop. Everything she knows about her own family begins and ends in that year, and the two records of it disagree about who was present for it.

A household made entirely of people who did not descend from it: every member came from a lineage that stopped one gate short and had no cultivator left to produce. It is the third answer to the same shortage - buy, cull, adopt - and it is the only one that leaves a debt attached to everybody.

reference_stats.summary: A seventh-gate mind practitioner with a defensive continuous burn: no spike, no window, no gap and no rest. She is warm, unshakeable and completely unspecialised, which makes her very hard to kill and very hard to rely on.

reference_stats.combat_read: Make her commit. She is built to hold and will hold for as long as the room lasts, but a continuous burn cannot spike, so anything that requires one decisive exchange is an answer. Otherwise there is nothing here: she cannot be shaken, cannot be worn down in a visible way, and cannot be frightened by anything that works on fear. The only thing she will lose is a fight somebody else starts badly.
notes: Her reference_stats describe a grant rather than a fighter: a defensive continuous burn is a slower fire and not a bigger one.
The single figure she cannot produce for anybody is her own name, and it is on both records under different ones.

identity.realm: the eighth gate at the liver, which is the last ordinary meridian and the first organ the grit kills

appearance.presentation: A grey-skinned man with the settled stillness of somebody breathing air that would kill a softer body in a season, and a fine dark dust in every crease of his clothing that never shakes out. He carries the mountain in his blood and it is written on his liver.
appearance.age: One hundred and forty-one. An ashwalker span, long enough that the load has had time to settle.
appearance.build: Barrel-chested, heavy through the hips and thick in the forearm, with the frame of somebody built to hold a load in bad air and to keep holding it.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown, waxy and slightly translucent at the ear, with the dark capillary bloom of a suspended mineral load visible along both forearms.
appearance.hair: Coarse black, worn short, and permanently dulled at the ends by the same dust that is in his collar.
appearance.eyes: Pale amber and heavily lidded, with the particular flat attention of somebody who is used to looking at a moving mass rather than at a face.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, scorched brown, black wool, and one band of guild orange at the left wrist - the only colour the spoil tally allows, so the tally can be read on a moving body.
appearance.attire: A heavy canvas and leather haul coat with a cloth mask pulled down at the throat, high-collared, sleeves bound to the wrist, and a tally board on a cord across his back where a person is a weight not a distance.
appearance.marks: A grey bloom at the throat where the mask sits, and a permanent grit-line under each eye from a lifetime of breathing down.
appearance.bearing: Squat, unhurried and immensely still when he stops. He stands the way a load stands: planted, low, and with nothing wasted on presentation.

canon.role_in_story: His title is a figure. The Heap Clan holds no land under it at all - what it holds is a crew and a number on a public tally of spoil moved, and the number is the only title the plain will recognise. The tally is public because it is a weight and not a distance, and a weight is the one measurement this tier can support. He has moved spoil for thirty years from a heap that has not moved, because with no spatial law there is no process on which waste disperses and a spent seam is visible from outside. So his name, his household's debt and his working life are all one number, and a defector's name sits against a figure that only goes down.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the base of the heap with a tally board on his back and his hand flat on the nearest barrow, reading the ground rather than the board.
canon.lore: An Ashwalker breathes volcanic grit and keeps it: the mineral load in the blood settles on the liver first, and the liver is the last ordinary meridian, so the whole species stops at the eighth gate one step short of the reservoirs. The same grit occludes the fine vessels introspection needs, which is why the mind path is closed to them outright and cannot be developed. Qi is complete and durable because it is processed through the same filter as the air, and the body is genuinely dense under load. On the plains he is one of the very few people who can stand at the base of a forty-year heap and work in the air there, which is why the tier's only insured job is clearing a face.
history: Born into a household whose only property was a place on a public tally and the debt attached to it, which is a tenancy that holds no land under it at all.
Took the tally at eleven, because the clan counts members by figure and a child is a small figure, and spent four years moving barrows under a number that did not rise.
Inherited a figure with three generations of debt on it, because the price of leaving a heap crew is that you owe the heap you did not move and the tally stays up.
Was the only man in his crew to work a whole season at the base, where the air is what it is, and lost two of the eight who went in with him.
Began marking the face he wants with a line of stone and did not place it on any charter, which is the only way it can survive a change of guild.

personality.summary: Enormously patient, entirely without eloquence, and privately precise about a number that nobody has ever asked him to explain. He thinks in weights, has never once thought in distances, and is entirely at peace with that except when somebody tries.

never refuses a shift and has never asked what a shift is worth
leaves no debts with the crew, on the grounds that a debt is the only thing in this arrangement that grows
has been right about the face four times and has been argued out of it four times
mannerisms: sets both feet before he answers anything that requires an opinion
wipes the grit from a hand with the other wrist rather than shaking it
counts barrows by touch along a face he cannot see the top of
answers a question about land with a question about weight
motivations: wants the face marked in stone rather than in a charter, because the charters keep changing hands
wants his tally number to stop falling, once, before he is finished
wants the debt that came with the figure cleared and never re-inherited
flaws: his whole worth is a figure that only goes down, and he has never been able to argue that in public
cannot introspect at all and has no idea what that costs him in a conversation
the liver is already failing and every shift he works shortens the only thing he has left
cannot leave the heap, because leaving means owing the heap he did not move
believes the guild and the guild agrees with him, and neither has been tested
personality.voice: Few words, no adjectives, and figures where other people use nouns. He will give you a barrow count rather than an opinion and will wait for you to work out which one you asked for.
taboos: will not leave a crew while a figure is outstanding against it
will not state a depth, on the grounds that this tier cannot measure distance
will not take a shift at a face he has not personally stood at

relationships.note: The clan owns a place on a public tally and the debt attached to it, and nothing else: the price of leaving is that you owe the heap you did not move and the tally stays up, so a defector's name sits against a number that only goes down. His figure is his name, his inheritance and his obligation, and there is no document in which those are three separate things.

The prize is the ground beneath the heap, and it cannot be split because the heap is one body and the ore is under it: nobody may dig without removing it and nobody may remove it without digging. He has been removing it for thirty years and the heap has not moved, so he has personally demonstrated that the standoff has no instrument but exhaustion.

The guild that moves the spoil heap off the seam floor, which is the only remaining ore-costly job on the plains and exists only because a law is absent: with no spatial law there is no process on which waste disperses. His tally is what the guild is judged by and the guild is what his debt is owed to, so he has never once been able to leave a dispute.

The house underwrites a caravan against the road closing, and clearing a face is the only insured job on the plains because it is the only one whose failure would be visible rather than merely slow. He has been insured for eleven years and has never met a clerk, because the policy does not require a face.

The guild that works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, and the party opposite the spoilwright in the only standoff on the plains that has outlasted three charters. A withdrawal from clearing concedes nothing on the ground, so the face stays buried under whoever's spoil it is - and his spoil is the reason nobody can work it.

An unimprinted group is not weak, it is absent, and absence has three signatures; spatial law is unspent on the Mortal Plains, so distance is not conserved and no process disperses waste. That one absence is the whole reason a forty-year heap is still standing on the last unworked iron, and the whole reason a weight is a legal title.

A public count of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it, and the only accounting this tier can support because a weight is the one measurement it has. His figure is in it every period and it has gone down more often than up, and the crews are the only body that has ever audited him.

The sterile ground around the Exhausted Seam: spoil that has not moved in four decades because nothing on the plains can make waste disperse, in a belt of air that would damage softer tissue in a season. He breathes it every shift and it is the only reason he can stand there at all.

reference_stats.summary: A qi practitioner at the eighth gate in the only air on the plains that kills a softer body outright, and a frame that carries more than anybody else's. He is enormously strong, entirely immune to being shaken, and physically unable to leave the only work he is competent for.
strengths: breathes the air at the base of the heap, where nobody softer can stand for a shift
a dense frame that carries a load all day and does not tire

unmoved by fear, because there is no faculty for it in the body he has
weaknesses: the eighth gate is fixed: the liver is the last ordinary meridian and the grit kills it first
the mind path is closed outright, so nothing about him can be read from the inside

cannot say what he thinks, only what he has counted, which makes negotiation nearly impossible
reference_stats.combat_read: He is very strong, very hard to move and completely impossible to read from the inside, so nothing that works on intent will touch him. Do not try to tire him out either; the frame does not tire. The one thing that beats an ashwalker is air - take him away from the heap and put him somewhere the grit is not, and the body that can breathe anything else will not be the one standing in front of you.
notes: His reference_stats describe a body whose only real weakness is a location, which is the entire condition of the tier's one insured job.
The number that is his name has fallen more often than it has risen in thirty years, and every shift he works moves it.
